audit_findings.title: The anchor and cash bridge use different business perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: VMS OE unquantified; filed 2025 VMS sales were less than $310.2m, sale proceeds were $160.3m, and proceeds equal $0.64 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor includes VMS operations and potentially disposal charges, while the latest cash bridge may retain the sale proceeds after the business left the forecast perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated results of operations presented below include the VitaFusion and L’il Critters brands which were sold to Piping Rock Health Products, Inc. on December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its net valuation effect is not. Removing VMS earnings lowers value, excluding nonrepeatable disposal costs raises value, and retaining sale proceeds in cash is appropriate only after VMS earnings are removed. Filed sales and proceeds do not establish VMS owner earnings, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Build filed 2025 OE separately for the surviving business and VMS, remove the latter and qualifying disposal costs, reconcile the $160.3m proceeds through the June 2026 cash roll-forward, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A non-cash impairment may have manufactured the volatility used to set growth
audit_findings.magnitude: $357.1m pre-tax, equal to 54.4% of reported 2024 OE and 169.0% of the $211.3m 2023-to-2024 OE decline
audit_findings.mechanism: If the impairment remained in 2024 OE, it artificially depressed the historical series and influenced the too-hard flag and bear/base/bull growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: VMS trade name and other asset impairment charges were $357.1 in 2024 related to non-cash charges to reduce the carrying value of intangible assets and property, plant, and equipment related to the VMS business.
audit_findings.explanation: The impairment and its size are demonstrated; whether the OE schedule neutralized it is unresolved. Because the charge exceeds the entire reported OE decline and the growth ruling expressly relies on that decline and rebound, retention is reasonably capable of changing the growth conclusion and valuation.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $357.1m through net income, operating cash flow and every 2024 OE adjustment. If any portion remains in OE, correct the series and rerun the trend, too-hard determination, growth scenarios and valuation.

audit_findings.title: Touchland is only partially represented in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $62.3m of 2024 annual-sales run rate omitted from the pre-acquisition portion of FY2025; OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor includes Touchland only from July 16, although forecast years and the post-acquisition balance sheet represent full ownership.
audit_findings.evidence: The Touchland acquisition is included in our results since July 16, 2025, the date of acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-year perimeter is demonstrated. The supplied filing gives $115.0m of 2024 annual sales but no stand-alone owner earnings, maintenance capital expenditure or full-year 2025 profitability, so the record cannot establish the valuation magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Obtain filed or transaction-supported Touchland results for January 1 through July 15, 2025, derive owner earnings without management forecasts, normalize the anchor to a full year, and rerun all scenarios without duplicating acquisition liabilities already paid.

audit_findings.title: The latest anchor may retain nonrepeatable exit charges
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum $34.5m post-tax, 4.0% of the $861.6m anchor and approximately $1.95 per share in the BASE valuation
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained nonrepeatable charge reduces anchor OE and is capitalized through the operating-value forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: We recorded a pre-tax charge of $45.6 (post-tax of $34.5) in 2025 as a direct result of these actions, of which $25.0 was recorded in Cost of sales and $20.6 was recorded in SG&A.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention in OE is unresolved, but the filed post-tax charge supplies a conservative maximum. Reversing the entire $34.5m would raise the base value from $49.66 to approximately $51.61 per share, still far below the $98.55 market price; inventory losses or already-added-back impairments would make the actual correction smaller.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $45.6m pre-tax charge among intangible and fixed-asset impairments and inventory losses, confirm existing OE add-backs, and rerun only for the portion both retained and demonstrably nonrecurring.

audit_findings.title: A committed common-share issuance is absent from the dilution ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: $50.0m filed award value, equal to 0.4% of the $12,360m base equity value; issuable share count unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The omitted shares would increase the fully diluted denominator while the associated compensation expense remains in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Company granted rights to Touchland’s founder to receive shares of our Common Stock valued at $50.0, with 50% of such shares vesting at each of the first and second year anniversaries of the closing.
audit_findings.explanation: The committed equity claim is demonstrated, although its share count is not. Its filed $50.0m value is only 0.4% of base equity value and cannot bridge the $48.89 per-share gap between base value and market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion on the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the award agreement or vesting disclosure, calculate the maximum shares issuable under its pricing formula, add them to the dilution ceiling, and recompute per-share values without reversing compensation expense.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.4m in 2021, $29.6m in 2022 and $28.1m in 2023; each is 3.3%-3.5% of the $861.6m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would be added back to historical OE and could modestly affect the trend or growth assessment, but no supplied residual applies to the 2025 anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2021 $30.4m (13.9% of filed D&A); FY2022 $29.6m (13.5% of filed D&A); FY2023 $28.1m (12.5% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The conservative exclusion is demonstrated, while eligibility remains unresolved. Even full historical add-backs would raise the already-higher $886m trend rather than the $861.6m latest-year anchor because the method uses the lower amount; the identified residuals therefore do not change the current anchor or valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed asset schedules and rerun the historical trend only for demonstrated eligible components; reopen materiality if comparable unrecognized amounts are found in 2024 or 2025.
